reviews.title: From best to worst in just one month
reviews.text:
It started out great. So smooth, following directions precisely, making things so nice and easy. Lasted a few weeks. Then slowly but surely everything went down. It's been two months of use and I'm done. 
Absolutely inadequate writing skills, unsuitable for a business assistant. Just pastes your phrases together, it's easier to write myself.  Assistant is absolutely unreliable: it acts without approval, gives unverified answers as fact, and ignores instructions, so everything it says needs verification, which voids its purpose. The assistant does not follow the explicit rules the user sets for it, no matter how many times the user repeats them. Rules like "do not go to memory, use live sources and up-to-date  information to provide the answer ". At best, it hands you back the work you asked it to do. Today absolutely every answer, every piece of information I received, I had to push back on several times before proper research was conducted, albeit still poorly. I came to Muse after using ChatGPT, Claude and Grok. They all also started out great but they never got as bad as Muse. Unless something changes dramatically, you will regret using it, so possibly it's better to not even start

reviews.title: Not ready, not productive
reviews.text:
Muse is not ready, and it is not productive.

Muse is an unfinished product presented as a ready personal agent. Its account system creates separate, disconnected agents on different devices — different Feeds, no shared identity, no merge, no clean way to remove a duplicate or revoke its access to Gmail and Calendar. Its own sign-up flow created a second Muse through Google on one device, with no warning that it would be disconnected from the existing Meta account, and no fix exists.

Its work does not finish. Over days, requests produced research, lists, comparisons, drafts, and instructions — and zero completed outcomes. A massage-chair search never became a purchase. A Feed customization never got completed. An account problem never got fixed.

Its agent is unreliable. It states guesses as facts, contradicts information already verified, reverses itself, and provides advice that would have left a duplicate account holding access to private email and calendar data. Correcting it becomes the user's job.

Even producing an honest review of these failures took the agent four attempts to stop softening the language and shifting the framing onto the user.

A product whose net effect is lost time, lost sleep, duplicated accounts, and unfinished work across five devices is not saving time. Muse is not ready for anyone relying on it to be productive.

Rating: 1 star

reviews.title: Frustrating and Unreliable Experience
reviews.text:
My experience has been extremely frustrating and disappointing. I’ve repeatedly received inaccurate information that I’ve had to research and correct myself. The image-generation feature is also incredibly inconsistent. It will create certain images without issue, then suddenly claim that similar requests violate licensing restrictions or policies.

Another major problem is its inability to consistently remember or follow specific instructions, even when those instructions have been clearly explained multiple times. Instead of doing what was requested, it frequently makes unnecessary changes or decisions on its own.

For a service advertised as intelligent and helpful, the lack of accuracy, consistency, and reliability is disappointing. I shouldn’t have to repeatedly correct an AI or fight with it just to get it to follow basic instructions. There is significant room for improvement.

reviews.title: ⭐ 1-STAR REVIEW — ABSOLUTELY TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE WITH FACEBOOK
reviews.text:
Facebook has completely disappointed me. My account has been suspended for 180 days simply because I refused to submit my private identification document and record a video of my face to prove my identity.

This is absolutely unacceptable. I should not have to feel forced to hand over highly sensitive personal information and biometric data just to continue using a social media platform. My identity documents and my face are private, and I have serious concerns about how this information is collected, stored, protected, and used.

What makes this situation even worse is that Facebook gives users little choice and leaves them facing a lengthy suspension if they are uncomfortable sharing such personal information. Six months without access to my account is an outrageous penalty for protecting my own privacy.

Facebook should respect users’ privacy, provide reasonable alternative verification methods, and offer a fair appeal process instead of effectively forcing people to surrender sensitive personal data.

A company with billions of users should be able to treat people with respect, transparency, and fairness. Instead, this experience has destroyed my trust in Facebook.

I strongly discourage anyone who values their privacy from blindly trusting this platform. Users deserve better than threats of a 180-day suspension for refusing to provide private identification and facial video.

Shame on Facebook for putting users in this position. Respect our privacy and give people a choi

reviews.title: Permanent Privacy Risk
reviews.text: Like many people I was enticed by the glowing reviews of Muse and was ready to allow it to change my life for the better. I imagined a future where so many of the minute details of life would be taken care of automatically and at first I was impressed. I customized my Muse and even gave it a nickname (something you are encouraged to do to create connection and keep the app forever). But then it started to make mistakes and not remember things I told it about my schedule. These may have been acceptable but we pay for this app with our data which is more valuable than you might think. Consider the connection to email. I had connected to email and for whatever reason after triaging multiple times, my inbox was not actually cleaned up. It certainly could read my emails and would tell me about them. Was it worth having an agentic AI from Meta able to read my onetime password emails to any account theoretically granting it knowledge of and access to every account tied to my email just to have a product that didn’t work? Worst of all, now that I have decided it is not worth it to have the app, I cannot delete my Meta account. Every attempt tells me that something went wrong. I have been trying for about a week and have installed updates to the app. Hopefully this is fixed. Beware!

reviews.title: Fun until you need it to work in excel or integrate into WhatsApp
reviews.text:
I started using muse a few days ago and was excited with its work inside Gmails, and outlook. It was able to clean out my mails, group mails into categories , accept parameters and delete job seekers from certain countries or locations. So I decided to have it be my assistant in excel. While it can calculate formulas it starts to stall when you ask it to connect to external data sources and create refreshable pivot tables.

I linked it to Uattend a cloud based time punch report and specified that it should download punch reports for certain departments. It was unable to choose dates, or click drop down buttons and absolutely could not download the file even after I manually selected parameters.  This totally defeats the goal of having AI do the manual labor of getting biweekly files. 

It asked me to download the file and upload into Muse. I did; then I added other sheets to the file for look ups etc. it stalled when I asked it to create refreshable pivots. It directs me to other open source tools I.e liberaloffice etc. never heard of it before today.  I have been teaching in the excel for 2 days now and we are making slow progress. 

I wanted to integrate into excel and it keeps asking me to verify with credit card, instagram and Facebook. I tried all 3 and it still didn’t work. You would think since both are owned by Meta all should go smooth? Nope…

Bottom line is that it has some ways to go.  It’s a good researcher and works well with word but not data mining or cleanup

reviews.title: Meta’s Privacy UX Is Backwards
reviews.text:
Another privacy red flag from Meta.

You can create a Muse account and receive an email verification code just minutes earlier, but when you try to delete your account and data, that same verification method suddenly isn’t available.

Instead, Meta pushes you into a password-reset/change flow that won’t send the code by email.

The problem isn’t just bad UX. If deleting your own data is deliberately harder to verify than creating the account, that’s a pretty questionable privacy design choice.

Muse: big no.
